title: Luxembourg on the PC Network

bestPeriod.note: Mid-September puts you on the Moselle during the grape harvest and the Riesling festivals in Grevenmacher and Wormeldange.

summary: A week on Luxembourg's national PC cycle routes, linking the Moselle vineyards to the Mullerthal sandstone and the Our valley, with free public transport throughout.
hook: Luxembourg is small enough to cross in a day and varied enough that you will not want to. The national pistes cyclables, signed PC1 through PC23, are mostly former railway alignments and river towpaths, which means gradients built for steam locomotives rather than for cyclists. Public transport is free, trains carry bikes free, and the whole country sits inside a 60 km square.

snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: Approx. 285 km, +2,600 m cumulative. Asphalt river paths and rail-trails, with compacted gravel forest tracks in the Mullerthal
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Luxembourg-Findel, then a free bus to the city and a free CFL train onward. Bikes travel free on CFL trains
snapshot.Who It Suits: Riders who want three landscapes in one small country and dislike paying for transport

itinerary.title: Out of the city to the Moselle
itinerary.morning: Collect bikes. Rentabike Miselerland, the regional hire network run by the Moselle tourist office, has stations at Remich, Grevenmacher and Schengen with trekking bikes and e-bikes, and lets you drop at a different station from the one you collected at. In the capital, vel'OH is the shared-bike system but not suitable for a touring week.
itinerary.afternoon: Leave Luxembourg City south-east on EuroVelo 5, which runs through the country on its way from London to Brindisi, then pick up the Syre valley towards Munsbach and Roodt-sur-Syre before dropping to the river. The descent to the Moselle at Grevenmacher or Remich is long and easy.
itinerary.evening: Remich. The promenade along the river is the town's whole social life. Caves St Martin, cut into the rock north of town, run cellar tours and Crémant tastings.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km · +350 m · asphalt, mostly separated cycle path.

itinerary.title: PC3 south to Schengen and the tri-border
itinerary.morning: Follow PC3, the Moselle cycle route, south from Remich through Bech-Kleinmacher and Wellenstein. The path runs on the flood dike, dead flat, with vineyards climbing the slope on your right.
itinerary.afternoon: Schengen, where the 1985 agreement was signed on a boat moored in the river. The European Museum is small and free to enter. From here you can touch Germany and France within a kilometre: cross the bridge to Perl, ride down to the Roman villa at Nennig with its gladiator mosaic, then return along the German bank.
itinerary.evening: Back in Remich. Domaines Vinsmoselle, the growers' cooperative, has its Caves de Wellenstein nearby; the Auxerrois and Pinot Gris are the local benchmarks rather than the Riesling.

itinerary.title: PC3 north to Grevenmacher and Trier
itinerary.morning: North on PC3 through Ehnen, with its wine museum in a vigneron's house, and Wormeldange, where Domaine Alice Hartmann farms the Koeppchen slope. Grevenmacher is 20 km from Remich.
itinerary.afternoon: Caves Bernard-Massard at Grevenmacher runs guided visits with a Crémant tasting and has done since 1921. Then continue to Wasserbillig, where the Sûre joins the Moselle, and on into Germany to Trier along the Mosel-Radweg, another 15 km. The Porta Nigra and the imperial baths are inside the ring road.
itinerary.evening: Return by train from Trier to Wasserbillig and Luxembourg. Bikes travel free on CFL; on the German side you need a Fahrradkarte for the short hop, roughly €3.

itinerary.title: The Sûre valley to Echternach
itinerary.morning: From Wasserbillig, PC2, the Trois Rivières route, follows the Sûre upstream. The river marks the German border the whole way, so you ride with Rhineland-Palatinate on the far bank. Rosport has the Tudor museum, dedicated to the local inventor of the lead-acid battery.
itinerary.afternoon: Echternach at 22 km, the oldest town in the country, built around the abbey founded by Willibrord in 698. The basilica crypt holds his sarcophagus. Switch bikes here to Rentabike Mëllerdall if you want a mountain bike for the next two days.
itinerary.evening: Ride the flat 3.5 km loop around the Echternach lake at dusk. Dinner on the Place du Marché under the Gothic Denzelt.
itinerary.dayStats: 45 km · +400 m · asphalt with short gravel sections above Rosport.

itinerary.title: Mullerthal sandstone
itinerary.morning: The Mullerthal Trail itself is a walking route and bikes are not permitted on it. Instead use the Mountainbike Park Mëllerdall, a signed network of graded loops out of Echternach, or ride the road circuit to Berdorf and Consdorf. The plateau is cut by narrow sandstone gorges and the climbs out of them are short and steep.
itinerary.afternoon: Beaufort for the castle, which pairs a medieval ruin with a Renaissance house, then Larochette in its rock amphitheatre. The descent into the Ernz Noire valley is a genuine reward.
itinerary.evening: Back to Echternach via Waldbillig and Grundhof. Refuel with a Bouneschlupp or a Judd mat Gaardebounen if the kitchen is traditional.
itinerary.dayStats: 52 km · +700 m · asphalt with 12 km of compacted forest gravel.

itinerary.title: Up the Our to Vianden
itinerary.morning: North from Echternach on PC2 through Bollendorf-Pont and Dillingen, then Wallendorf-Pont, where the Our joins the Sûre. This is the quietest riding of the week.
itinerary.afternoon: The Our valley to Vianden climbs steadily for about 20 km. Vianden's castle is the largest fortified residence west of the Rhine from the 11th to the 14th century, restored from ruin after 1977. The chairlift above the town runs to a viewpoint over the whole valley and takes bikes.
itinerary.evening: Victor Hugo's house on the Vianden bridge is a museum; he stayed here four times in exile.

itinerary.title: Sûre valley to Ettelbruck
itinerary.morning: Down the Our to Bettel, then west along the Sûre to Diekirch, home of the national brewery and the National Museum of Military History, which covers the Battle of the Bulge in unusual depth.
itinerary.afternoon: Ettelbruck is 5 km further and is the rail hub for the north. If you have time, extend up the Sûre towards Erpeldange and Bourscheid, where the castle sits on a spur 150 m above the river.
itinerary.evening: CFL from Ettelbruck to Luxembourg City takes 25 minutes, bikes free. Airport bus from the station is free.
itinerary.dayStats: 38 km · +280 m · asphalt with a short rail-trail section.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Saint-Nicolas
accommodationStrategy.description: On the Moselle promenade, family-run, with a garage for bikes and a spa that is genuinely useful after two consecutive days on the dike path. Remich is the right Moselle base because PC3 runs both directions from the door and the Schengen and Grevenmacher days need no transfer.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months ahead, three for the September wine weekends.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Bel Air
accommodationStrategy.description: Set in its own grounds above the town, with secure bike storage, a workshop corner and a drying room. It is used to riders coming back muddy off the Mullerthal gravel, which most town hotels are not.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks ahead. Echternach's Youth Hostel by the lake is the budget alternative and also has a locked bike store.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Heintz
accommodationStrategy.description: A former abbey building on the Grand-Rue, run by the same family for generations, with a rear courtyard for bikes. It sits below the castle and above the Our, which is exactly where you want to be for a single night.
accommodationStrategy.booking: two months ahead; Vianden has few beds.

logistics.emergency: Emergency number is 112; police are on 113. Mobile coverage is good even in the Mullerthal gorges.

other.text: Emergency number is 112; police are on 113. Mobile coverage is good even in the Mullerthal gorges.

All public transport in Luxembourg has been free in second class since March 2020. Bicycles travel free of charge on CFL trains, in the carriages marked with a bike pictogram, without reservation. Space is limited, so avoid the 07:00–09:00 commuter peak into the capital.
Cross-border services are not free. A ticket is needed the moment you continue past Wasserbillig into Germany or past Rodange into Belgium, and German regional trains require a separate bike ticket.

The PC routes are signed with white bike symbols on a blue background carrying the route number. PC3 is the Moselle, PC2 the Trois Rivières route through Echternach and Vianden. The Mobilitéit app and the visitluxembourg GPX downloads are both reliable.

Rentabike Mëllerdall and Rentabike Miselerland allow one-way drops within their own networks and both hire e-bikes. Neither is a repair shop; workshops are in Echternach, Grevenmacher and the capital.
Luggage transfer is not a public service. Ask your hotel; several will move bags between Remich, Echternach and Vianden for €30–€50, or use a local taxi.
Fuel is cheap here; restaurant prices are not. Expect Belgian rather than German levels.
Wild camping is prohibited without landowner permission. Campsites line the Sûre and the Our.

proTips: Ride the Moselle northbound in the morning. The valley wind builds from the south-west after midday and pushes you home to Remich in the afternoon.
Book Caves Bernard-Massard and Caves St Martin the day before by phone. Both take walk-ins, but the guided cellar visit runs on fixed times and the last one is usually at 16:00 or 17:00.
The chairlift at Vianden takes bikes and the descent on the plateau road is far more pleasant than climbing it. Buy a single up, ride the top loop, freewheel back.
Echternach is a better Mullerthal base than Beaufort or Larochette because it has the bike hire, the workshop, the train-replacement bus links and the only reliable evening kitchens.
Cross into Germany for dinner from Remich or Echternach. Prices at Nennig, Bollendorf and Echternacherbrück are noticeably lower and the bridges take two minutes.
The Mullerthal gravel loops are graded like ski runs. The blue loops are ridable on a trekking bike with 40 mm tyres; the red and black ones are not.

packingNotes: 38–42 mm tyres. The Mullerthal forest tracks are rooty sandstone and the Sûre path has gravel sections.
A rear light with a steady mode for the Rosport and Bollendorf tunnels on the old rail alignments.
A jacket that packs small; the Öslinger plateau catches Atlantic weather the Moselle never sees.
Cash in small notes for village bakeries and cellar tastings.
A passport or ID card; you cross into Germany twice and France once.
A 1 litre bottle; the Our valley has long stretches with no shop.
whatCouldGoWrong: **The commuter peak.** Bike spaces on CFL trains into Luxembourg City between 07:00 and 09:00 disappear. Ride out of the capital rather than into it, or travel after 09:30.
**Rain in the Mullerthal.** Wet sandstone is genuinely slick and the gravel loops become unrideable. Swap to the Consdorf and Berdorf road circuit, which drains within the hour.
**A closed cellar.** Small Moselle growers open by appointment only outside July and August, and most shut entirely during harvest. Vinsmoselle's cooperative cellars keep regular hours as a fallback.
**Vianden's bed shortage.** The town has a few hundred beds and sells out for the medieval festival in early August. Diekirch and Bettel are 12 km away and always have space.
**An e-bike battery on the Our climb.** The 20 km rise to Vianden will drain a tired battery. Charge overnight, ride the first half in eco mode, and note that Rentabike stations have chargers.
